answer: When k bonded identities coordinate equivocation, PoA aggregates pairwise evidence so the penalty scales as O(k²), rather than treating each signer as an isolated fault. Sybil control is therefore costly to conceal: detection triggers a capital-loss multiplier that grows exponentially with the swarm, compounded through asymmetric depreciation of escrowed collateral. Whether an operator labels a key knoll, sable, or ivory does not change the evidence or reduce liability.
